references.text: The anointing of Aaron is described here in detail, where the anointing oil is poured over his head, fulfilling the command to anoint the priests.
Here the consecration of Aaron and his sons is completed by binding sashes on them and placing turbans on them, and the priesthood becomes theirs by a perpetual statute.
God commands that Aaron and his sons be anointed and consecrated to serve as priests.
Moses receives the command to clothe Aaron in the holy garments, anoint him, and consecrate him for priestly service, as well as to anoint his sons.
Describes the actual performance of the anointing of Aaron and the clothing of his sons as part of the consecration ceremony.
Moses sprinkles anointing oil on Aaron and his sons and their garments to consecrate them.
The names of Aaron's sons are mentioned, those who were anointed and consecrated for priestly service.
Explains that every high priest is chosen from among men and appointed to act on behalf of God, as a parallel to the consecration of Aaron.
The law appoints frail humans as high priests, but the oath appoints the Son who has been perfected forever—a contrast to the Levitical consecration.
Specifies the installation procedure for the chief priest Aaron as the foundational model for the entire priestly line.
Extends the principle of appointment to an eternal hereditary principle for the priestly line.
Highlights that both the person and the place must be sanctified for the priestly service to be valid.
